description: The statistical modelling toolkit behind most applied data work, from least squares to generalised linear and mixed-effects models. Students derive the estimators, fit and diagnose models on African health, agriculture and economic data, and quantify prediction error with cross-validation and the bootstrap.
modelledOn: James, Witten, Hastie and Tibshirani, An Introduction to Statistical Learning
Kutner, Nachtsheim, Neter and Li, Applied Linear Statistical Models
Agresti, Foundations of Linear and Generalized Linear Models
Gelman and Hill, Data Analysis Using Regression and Multilevel/Hierarchical Models
outcomes: Derive the least squares estimator in matrix form and state the assumptions behind its inference.
Fit, interpret and test simple and multiple regression models including categorical predictors and interactions.
Diagnose violations such as non-constant variance, influential points and collinearity, and apply remedies.
Select and regularise models using information criteria, ridge, lasso and cross-validation.
Fit logistic, Poisson and other generalised linear models and interpret coefficients, deviance and overdispersion.
Model clustered data with random effects and quantify uncertainty with the bootstrap.

units.title: Simple linear regression
topics: Least squares for one predictor: normal equations and the geometric view as projection
Properties of the estimators: unbiasedness, variance and the Gauss-Markov theorem
Inference: t-tests, confidence and prediction intervals, the ANOVA table and R-squared
Correlation versus regression, regression to the mean and the hazards of extrapolation
Transformations: log-log models and elasticities, Box-Cox

units.title: Multiple linear regression
topics: Matrix formulation: the estimator (X'X)^-1 X'y, the hat matrix and degrees of freedom
Partial coefficients, adjusted R-squared and the F-test for nested models
Categorical predictors, dummy coding and interaction terms
Polynomial terms, splines and basis expansions
Confounding, omitted-variable bias and Simpson's paradox

units.title: Diagnostics and remedies
topics: Residual plots for linearity, constant variance, normality and independence
Leverage, Cook's distance, DFFITS and influential observations
Multicollinearity: variance inflation factors and condition numbers
Heteroscedasticity: Breusch-Pagan test, weighted least squares and robust sandwich standard errors
Autocorrelated errors and the Durbin-Watson test

units.title: Model selection and regularisation
topics: Best subset and stepwise selection; AIC, BIC and Mallows' Cp
Ridge regression: shrinkage, bias-variance trade-off and the closed form
Lasso and elastic net: sparsity, the geometry of the penalty and coordinate descent
Choosing the penalty by cross-validation and the one-standard-error rule
Principal components regression and partial least squares

units.title: Logistic regression and classification
topics: Binary responses, odds and the logit link; maximum likelihood fitted by iteratively reweighted least squares
Interpreting coefficients as odds ratios; Wald and likelihood-ratio tests
Deviance, goodness of fit and the Hosmer-Lemeshow test
Classification performance: confusion matrix, ROC curve, AUC, calibration and threshold choice
Multinomial and ordinal logistic regression
Separation, sparse data and rare events

units.title: Generalised linear models
topics: The exponential family and GLM framework: linear predictor, link and variance function
Poisson regression for counts; offsets for exposure and rate models
Overdispersion: quasi-Poisson and negative binomial regression
Binomial grouped data and gamma regression for positive skewed outcomes
Iteratively reweighted least squares for the general GLM and its convergence
Residuals, deviance and checking the link and variance assumptions

units.title: Mixed-effects and hierarchical models
topics: Clustered and repeated data: intraclass correlation and why ordinary least squares understates error
Random intercepts and slopes; REML estimation and best linear unbiased predictors
Partial pooling and shrinkage in hierarchical models of clinics, schools or villages
Generalised linear mixed models and model comparison
Longitudinal data: growth curves and missing observations

units.title: Resampling, prediction error and reporting
topics: Cross-validation: k-fold, leave-one-out shortcut for linear models and nested cross-validation
The bootstrap: case and residual resampling, percentile and BCa intervals
Prediction error: optimism, bias-variance decomposition and expected prediction error
Reproducible workflow and communicating uncertainty to non-statisticians
Capstone analysis of a real dataset such as cocoa yields, malaria incidence or household survey spending

schedule.title: Least squares and inference for one predictor
schedule.exercise: Derive the least squares slope and intercept, prove they are unbiased and compute a 95 percent confidence interval for the slope from a small table of data by hand.

tasks.title: Fit a line to ten rainfall and maize yield pairs by the normal equations, plot residuals and verify that they sum to zero
Fit a simple regression in R, read the ANOVA table and check that R-squared equals the squared correlation and F equals t squared
Simulate 5,000 samples to show the slope estimator is unbiased, compare its variance with theory and see how it shrinks with n

schedule.title: Correlation, regression to the mean and transformations
schedule.exercise: Explain regression to the mean using exam scores or repeated clinic measurements, and write a paragraph on why extrapolating a fitted line is risky.

tasks.title: Simulate two exam scores with correlation 0.5 and show that the top decile falls back toward the mean on retest
Fit a log-log model of household food spending on income, interpret the slope as an elasticity and compare residuals with the untransformed fit
Choose a Box-Cox transformation for skewed hospital stay lengths by profile likelihood and judge the improvement with residual plots

schedule.title: Matrix form of multiple regression
schedule.exercise: Show that the hat matrix is symmetric and idempotent, and use it to explain leverage and the degrees of freedom of the fit.

tasks.title: Compute beta from (X'X)^-1 X'y for a 12-row, 3-predictor dataset using the matrix tools and check the residuals are orthogonal to the columns of X
Compare nested models with the F-test and adjusted R-squared on a crop-yield dataset and explain which predictors earn their place
Compute the hat matrix of a design, plot leverage values and find which row can move the fitted line the most

schedule.title: Categorical predictors, interactions and confounding
schedule.exercise: Using a worked example, explain how omitting a confounder can reverse the sign of a coefficient, and state what a regression can and cannot say about causation.

tasks.title: Fit a model of farm income with region as a dummy-coded factor, interpret each coefficient and plot predicted means with intervals
Fit polynomial and cubic spline terms to the age and height relationship of children and choose the flexibility by an F-test
Build a dataset exhibiting Simpson's paradox with two clinics and show the reversed slopes in pooled and stratified regressions

schedule.title: Diagnostics: residuals, influence, collinearity
schedule.exercise: Given a fitted model and its four diagnostic plots, write a short diagnosis of each violation you can see and propose a remedy.

tasks.title: Produce the four standard residual plots for a fitted housing price model and name the assumption each one checks
Add one extreme point to a dataset, compute Cook's distance and DFFITS, and show how the slope changes when it is removed
Detect heteroscedasticity with the Breusch-Pagan test on income data, then compare ordinary, weighted and robust standard errors

schedule.title: Model selection and regularisation
schedule.exercise: Compare subset selection, ridge and lasso on one dataset in a table of test error, number of variables and stability, and say which you would trust.

tasks.title: Run best subset and forward stepwise selection on eight predictors and compare AIC, BIC and Cp in choosing the model size
Compute ridge estimates for a range of penalties on correlated predictors and plot the coefficient paths to see the shrinkage
Fit the lasso with ten-fold cross-validation on 40 predictors, report which coefficients are zero and compare the test error with ridge

schedule.title: Logistic regression
schedule.exercise: Interpret a logistic regression of loan default on income and mobile-money usage, giving odds ratios with intervals and a plain-language reading of each.

tasks.title: Do two iterations of iteratively reweighted least squares for a tiny logistic problem by hand and compare with the fitted values from code
Fit a logistic model of malaria status on bed net use and age, report odds ratios with intervals and test a coefficient by Wald and likelihood ratio
Compare nested logistic models by deviance, run the Hosmer-Lemeshow test and say whether the fit is adequate

schedule.title: Classification performance and extensions
schedule.exercise: Choose a decision threshold for a clinic screening model by weighing the cost of a missed case against the cost of an unnecessary follow-up, and justify it.

tasks.title: Compute the confusion matrix, ROC curve and AUC for a fitted classifier and mark the threshold that maximises Youden's index
Fit a multinomial model of transport mode choice for commuters and interpret one coefficient as a relative risk ratio
Reproduce complete separation in a small dataset, observe the failing estimates and fix it with a Firth-type penalty

schedule.title: The GLM framework and Poisson regression
schedule.exercise: Show that the normal, binomial and Poisson distributions belong to the exponential family and identify the canonical link for each.

tasks.title: Write the Poisson and Bernoulli distributions in exponential-family form and read off the canonical link and variance function
Fit a Poisson model of clinic visit counts with a population offset and interpret the rate ratio for a district-level covariate
Test for overdispersion in a count dataset, compare quasi-Poisson and negative binomial fits and explain the effect on standard errors

schedule.title: Further GLMs and checking
schedule.exercise: Choose a GLM family and link for four outcomes (counts, proportions, claim sizes, binary events) and justify each with a data example.

tasks.title: Fit a gamma GLM with log link to insurance claim sizes and compare predictions with a log-transformed linear model
Implement iteratively reweighted least squares for a Poisson GLM in code and verify it matches the library fit to six decimals
Plot deviance and Pearson residuals for a fitted GLM and use a link test to decide whether to change the link function

schedule.title: Mixed-effects and hierarchical models
schedule.exercise: Analyse test scores from pupils nested in schools in a short report that compares pooled, unpooled and partially pooled estimates.

tasks.title: Compute the intraclass correlation for pupil scores within schools and show how ignoring clustering shrinks the standard errors
Fit a random intercept and random slope model for repeated child growth measurements and compare it with a fixed-effects fit
Show partial pooling by plotting each village's estimate under no pooling, complete pooling and the hierarchical model

schedule.title: Cross-validation, bootstrap and prediction error
schedule.exercise: Explain in a page why training error is optimistic, how cross-validation estimates test error and when the bootstrap interval can fail.

tasks.title: Implement k-fold cross-validation and the leave-one-out shortcut for a linear model and check the two give identical errors
Build percentile and BCa bootstrap intervals for a regression slope with skewed errors and compare with the t-based interval
Estimate squared bias and variance of a polynomial fit at several degrees by simulation and plot the resulting error curve

schedule.title: Reporting and capstone analysis
schedule.exercise: Deliver a reproducible analysis of a real dataset, including model choice, diagnostics, uncertainty and a half-page summary for a non-statistician.

tasks.title: Produce a reproducible notebook for a regression analysis with figures, a diagnostics section and a coefficient table with intervals
Model cocoa yield per farm from rainfall, fertiliser and farm size, choose between candidate models by cross-validation and justify the choice
Compare a GLM with a regularised model on a malaria incidence dataset and report test performance with bootstrap intervals and a recommendation
